ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $D$ is a point on side $AC$ of $\triangle ABC$. An arc is drawn with $A$ as the center and $AD$ as the radius, intersecting the extension line of $BA$ at point $E$, and $ED$ is connected. If $\angle B=60^\circ$ and $\angle C=70^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle ADE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $\angle B=60^\circ$ and $\angle C=70^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle CAB=180^\circ-\angle B-\angle C=50^\circ$,\\
since an arc is drawn with A as the center and AD as the radius, intersecting the extension of BA at point E,\\
it implies AE=AD,\\
thus $\angle AED=\angle ADE$,\\
since $\angle AED+\angle ADE=\angle CAB$,\\
therefore $\angle ADE+\angle ADE=50^\circ$,\\
which gives $\angle ADE=\boxed{25^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is triangle ABC, B is at the lower right, C is above, A is on the base line EB and is located between E and B; E is on the reverse extension line of BA. D is located on the slanted side AC from A to C, and segment ED has been connected. In the figure, the arc with A as the center passes through D and intersects the extension line of BA at E, indicating that AE and AD are radii of the same circle. Reasoning: Given ∠B=60° and ∠C=70°, and the sum of the interior angles of triangle ABC is 180°, so ∠CAB=180°−60°−70°=50°. Since AE and AB are on the same straight line and in opposite directions, while AD is along the direction of AC, the interior angle ∠EAD at A in △AED is 180°−∠CAB=180°−50°=130°. The arc construction gives AE=AD, therefore △AED is an isosceles triangle, and the base angles ∠AED=∠ADE. Thus ∠AED+∠ADE=180°−130°=50°, so each base angle is 50°÷2=25°. Therefore ∠ADE=25°.
